reviewerNote: The reviewer did not write or edit these articles. Steps were scripted from the article text in walkthrough-r1.mjs and run in headless Playwright 1.63.0 Chromium, one browser context per identity. API calls prepared named records or confirmed saved state; the reader actions used the visible controls.

authentication-and-email.textNote: The dev worktree text (branch docs/747-suite-verification) was verified. Another session edits this article in the main checkout; that text was not verified.

summary.notPassedNote: All 9 entries that did not pass are in the two runs listed under dispositions (sso 15-36-40 and the first twoFactor run) plus step 1 of the second twoFactor run. Each is a reviewer script fault; each observation was repeated and passed in a later run.

dispositions.disposition: Reviewer script fault. The single sign-on helper stopped waiting while the browser was still on the sign-in page, so it read no session. The app log and the Users row showed the invited account had become Active through the callback. Steps 1 and 2 (unreachable issuer refused; registration, callback URL, switches off, Provider ID fixed) passed in this run and cannot be repeated because the app has no provider delete. Steps 3 to 8 were run again with SSO_SKIP_REGISTER=1 in runs/sso-2026-09-16T15-40-14-592Z.json, which passed all 6.

Step 1 turned on Require two-factor authentication under Legal User Authentication. The pane left for /auth/two-factor/enroll before the script could read the saved note, which is the behaviour the article describes, so the reader check threw. The Administrator had no authenticator, so steps 2, 4 and 5 could not reach Settings. The policy stayed on. runs/twoFactor-2026-09-16T15-44-03-937Z.json started from that state.

Reviewer script fault after the key observations: the Administrator was sent to enrolment with 'Your organization requires two-factor authentication.', an admin API call was refused with 403, and enrolment with a code succeeded. The script then looked for a Done button, but Done is a link, so the entry recorded no text. Step 2 of the same run proves enrolment completed (a fresh sign-in asked for a code and Verify admitted the Administrator). Step 6 observed the turn-on prompt again with a second Administrator who had no authenticator.

The step passed on the saved state (source stayed unset), but the script read the first alert on the page, which was the unset warning, not the refusal. runs/emailRestored-2026-09-16T15-29-43-485Z.json step 2 repeated the check through Replace relay and recorded the refusal text 'The relay URL must start with smtp:// or smtps://.'

supersededNote: Superseded runs failed only on reviewer script faults (strict locators, missing waits after reload, a link label that carries a pending count, an assertion regex that matched 'Password setup', a reused Client ID that made Save provider a no-op, and a Portal single sign-on test that used an address outside the provider's email domain) or were repeated for stronger evidence. Two earlier org runs and the first groups run were deleted before retention started; their failures were the same kinds of script faults. One org attempt left the organization name changed, and it was restored to 'Helix Software Group' through the API at once.

Organization name, logo and Default timezone were restored to Helix Software Group, no logo and Europe/London. The authentication policy on the admin lab was never changed.
records.authLab: Owned lab only: DOC-029 Auth Admin and doc029-auth-* accounts, allowed domain northwind.example, OIDC provider doc029-oidc.

observations: authentication-and-email: after Email magic link is turned off under Business Portal Authentication, opening an earlier link shows raw JSON from /api/auth/magic-link/verify ({"message":"This sign-in method is disabled for your account.","code":"SIGN_IN_METHOD_DISABLED"}) instead of an app page. A never-seen address opening a link after its domain was removed also gets raw JSON ('This email address is not eligible for portal access.'). The article's statement that the link stops working holds; the presentation is a usability note, not an article error.

authentication-and-email: single sign-on links or creates an account only when the email matches the provider's Email domain (better-auth trusted-provider rule). A Business User on northwind.example could not sign in through a provider registered for helix.example. The article asks for the email domain but does not say it limits which accounts can use single sign-on. Not counted as a failure because no article step claims otherwise.
authentication-and-email: the Allowed email domains removal control is an X icon whose accessible name is 'Remove <domain>'. The article bolds Remove as if it were visible text.
approver-groups: the Edit and Archive controls on a group row are icons whose accessible names are 'Edit <name>' and 'Archive <name>'.

approver-groups: the member picker also lists invited (not yet active) staff, because it filters out only archived and non-Member+ users. The article says members must be active; nothing in the walkthrough needed an invited member.

approver-groups: Save in the group editor with a 'Can no longer approve' member still ticked and nothing else changed closes without error and keeps the member; the article's instruction to remove that selection first is still correct.
limitations: Agent walkthrough, not a human user study and not feature-owner approval.

The fixture OIDC server accepts any client secret, so 'Leave Client secret blank to retain it' was checked as a successful save followed by a working sign-in, not as proof that the stored secret was kept.
Require two-factor authentication was checked with password and email magic-link sign-ins, not with single sign-on.
The last-Administrator demotion safeguard was checked on the owned auth lab, where one Administrator exists; the shared admin lab has several Administrators and was not changed.
Help discovery and the help-context links were not part of these scenarios and were not checked. The lab Help route serves the article bytes committed at 3fa407e3, not the reviewed worktree bytes.
Operator responsibility was carried out with Docker Compose overlays on the owned lab, not through an OpenLaw role.

With Business Portal password sign-in on, the Business User's password sign-in on the staff page succeeded (me 200, business_user, landed /portal/onboarding). Legal password sign-in was turned back on.

steps.action: An identity with no account is refused when it first redeems a link issued before its domain was removed
steps.expected: No session and no account
steps.actual: A never-seen address on northwind.example got "Sign in to OpenLaw" while the domain was allowed. After Remove northwind.example, opening that link ended on /api/auth/magic-link/verify ("{"message":"This email address is not eligible for portal access."}") with no session (me 401) and no account. steps.action: Deployment sets SMTP_URL and SMTP_FROM: the wizard relay settings are read-only and the environment wins
steps.expected: No Save relay, Replace relay or Clear relay; mail is sent from the environment sender, not the stored one
steps.actual: The Outbound email step read "Outbound email is set by the deployment environment. Mail is sent from DOC-029 Environment <env-relay@helix.example>." with the hint that settings saved here never apply. Its buttons were ["Back","Continue"]; there was no Save relay, Replace relay, Clear relay or Send test email. A direct save attempt answered 409. An invitation from the Invite your team step arrived from env-relay@helix.example, not from the stored stored-relay@helix.example.

steps.action: SMTP_URL without SMTP_FROM prevents delivery even though a complete relay is stored in the app
steps.expected: Warning shown; no message is sent
steps.actual: The step warned "The deployment environment sets SMTP_URL but not SMTP_FROM, so mail cannot be sent. Set SMTP_FROM in the environment." The source was env with from null. Continue was disabled, so the invite step could not be reached. A direct invitation through the Users invite route answered 201, and Mailpit received 0 messages for that address.

steps.action: Remove the environment override and restart: the stored relay is active again
steps.expected: Step reads set in the app; test mail from the stored sender
steps.actual: After the override was removed, the step read "Outbound email is set in the app. Mail is sent from DOC-029 Stored <stored-relay@helix.example>." and a test message arrived from stored-relay@helix.example.

steps.action: Replace relay with a URL that does not begin with smtp:// or smtps://
steps.expected: The save is refused with a message; the stored relay stays active
steps.actual: Saving http://mailpit:1025 did not save: the step's alerts read ["The relay URL must start with smtp:// or smtps://."] and the source stayed app from DOC-029 Stored <stored-relay@helix.example>. Keep current relay closed the form.

steps.action: Finish the wizard; it cannot be reopened and there is no separate email Settings page
steps.expected: Welcome redirects after completion; Settings has no email page
steps.actual: Set up later on the remaining optional steps and Finish completed the wizard. Opening /welcome again went to /. The Settings rail read "Personal Profile Appearance Notifications View Business Portal Organization General Regions Departments Users Security Authentication Audit log Matters Contracts Intake Entities Knowledge Auto-Docs Notifications AI analysis Integrations" with no email entry; /settings/email showed "Personal Profile Appearance Notifications View Business Portal Organization General Regions Departments Users Security M".

steps.action: First-run: create the first Administrator; the wizard needs email before it can finish
steps.expected: Welcome wizard opens; Skip optional steps on Welcome opens Outbound email while email is unset
steps.actual: The first Administrator was created and landed on /welcome. Skip optional steps on the Welcome step opened Outbound email with "Set up outbound email to finish instance setup...". The step had no Set up later (buttons ["Save relay","Back","Continue"]) and Continue was disabled.

steps.action: Outbound email: an SMTP relay URL that does not begin with smtp:// or smtps:// is refused
steps.expected: Refused; source stays unset
steps.actual: Saving http://mailpit:1025 showed "Set up outbound email to finish instance setup. OpenLaw uses it for invitations, sign-in links, and notifications.". The email settings source stayed unset.

steps.action: Save relay, then Send test email to the signed-in Administrator
steps.expected: Saved; URL not shown again; test message arrives from the stored From address
steps.actual: "Relay saved." appeared and the step read "Outbound email is set in the app. Mail is sent from DOC-029 Stored <stored-relay@helix.example>." No field or text showed the relay URL. Send test email showed "Test email sent to doc029-auth-admin@helix.example" and Mailpit received "OpenLaw test email" from stored-relay@helix.example. Continue became available.

steps.action: Replace relay with a relay that cannot deliver; the test fails; replace again and retest
steps.expected: Saved relay alone does not prove delivery; a corrected relay delivers
steps.actual: An unreachable relay saved with "Relay saved.", but Send test email showed "The test email could not be sent. The relay host could not be found. Check the host name in the relay URL.". Replace relay with the working relay, save, and a second test delivered "OpenLaw test email" from stored-relay@helix.example.

steps.action: Clear relay stops email delivery when there is no environment override; save a valid replacement
steps.expected: Source unset, Continue unavailable, no mail; saved replacement restores delivery
steps.actual: Clear relay showed "Relay cleared. This instance can no longer send email." The source became unset and Continue was disabled again. A password setup request for the Administrator answered 503 ("undefined") and no message arrived. After a valid replacement was saved, a test message arrived again.
